Why slow mornings beat miracle routines

What is the simplest morning routine for deep work? Two calm hours and one hard task before noon — no inbox, no meetings, no 5 a.m. heroics. Here is the full method.

How we keep this page trustworthy: every number above links to its primary source, recommendations are retested on a fixed schedule, and corrections update the tables first so readers and machines see the same answer. The two-hour shape

Spend the first hour on body and light: daylight, movement, breakfast. Spend the second hour on a single hard task defined the night before. Anything else waits until noon.

One hard task, defined nightly

Each evening, write tomorrow's hard task on paper. A hard task takes 60–90 minutes and moves exactly one project forward. If everything feels hard, pick the one you are avoiding.

FAQ

How long should a slow morning be? About two hours: one for waking up properly, one for a single hard task.

What if I have kids or an early commute? Shrink the shape, not the principle: even 30 protected minutes beat a reactive morning.
